description: At most one fact row per country x indicator x year.
The fact has exactly the configured country x indicator x year combinations, none missing and none extra (missing values are rows with a status, not absent rows).
Every fact row joins to its country, indicator and year dimension rows.
The API returned more than one observation for the same country x indicator x year (the load keeps the first; the source needs investigating).
Observations whose year or value could not be parsed. They would otherwise look like missing data.
value_status agrees with the row: present <=> value not null; not_returned <=> no source response.
Every sourced fact row points to a raw response that belongs to the ingest run the core layer was built from.
Values lie within the plausible range configured per indicator.
GDP / population matches reported GDP per capita within the configured tolerance (see quality.v_gdp_per_capita_consistency).
Country x indicator x year combinations without a value (null in source or not returned). Expected for recent years; reported so the gaps are visible.
Every country in scope was described by the API, including its income group (needed for the income-group comparison; "not classified" counts as described).
Every configured focus country is in scope (in 'all' mode: listed by the API as an economy), so dashboards and the comparison year are based on real countries.
Every configured indicator was described by the API.
The API returned observations outside the configured scope (ignored by the load).
The historical income classification was loaded when configured; otherwise every year uses the current income group (see core.dim_country_income_year.income_group_source).

The historical classification covers the latest published data year that falls in the configured range (classifications for year Y appear each July of Y+1). An older edition means the configured URL points at a superseded workbook.
Every economy in scope appears in the historical classification for the years it covers (a missing economy falls back to its current group in those years).
The World Bank's lastupdated date is known and was no older than max_source_age_days when the data was fetched.
No ingest run has failed since the run being checked; otherwise the published data is older than intended.
